quotes.text: In my view, our current monetary policy stance is not sufficiently tight, which is why I voted in the last two meetings for a 25 basis point increase in Bank Rate.
Since then, the gap has widened further, implying over 100 basis points of tightening in Bank Rate over the coming 12 months.

I plot the estimated monetary policy uncertainty factor in the right panel of Chart 8, which shows that monetary policy uncertainty increased significantly following the March decision, which cannot simply be attributed to uncertainty around the economic outlook resulting from the conflict.
In my view, real financial conditions are insufficiently tight.

summary.text: Catherine Mann says she voted in the last two meetings for a 25 basis point increase in Bank Rate.

fragments.text: Since then, the gap has widened further, implying over 100 basis points of tightening in Bank Rate over the coming 12 months.

summary.text: Catherine Mann says the gap between the OIS curve and survey expectations widened further, implying over 100 basis points of tightening in Bank Rate over the coming 12 months.

fragments.text: According to this term structure model, higher term premia account for around 24 basis points of the increase in the UK, compared with just 4 basis points in Germany.

summary.text: Catherine Mann says the Bank’s updated short-term inflation forecast from September projects inflation to increase to over 4% in Q1 2027.

fragments.text: In my view, real financial conditions are insufficiently tight.

The appropriate response therefore is not to rely on risk premia to do the work of policy, but to reduce inflation risk and policy uncertainty through a clearly communicated reaction function and a sufficiently restrictive path for Bank Rate.

summary.text: Catherine Mann says real financial conditions are insufficiently tight and calls for a clearly communicated reaction function and a sufficiently restrictive path for Bank Rate.

quotes.text: However, inflation is too high and has exceeded the Federal Reserve's 2 percent target for more than five years.
I view that level as near maximum employment.
As my base case, I expect inflation to be elevated in the short run before resuming its decline toward our 2 percent goal as the effects of energy and other price shocks fade.
I supported that decision because I saw it as the appropriate policy to pursue the Fed's dual mandate.

fragments.text: I see the economy as likely to show continued resilience, despite these challenges, by adding jobs and extending a six-and-a-half-year-long expansion.

summary.text: Governor Jefferson says the economy is likely to show continued resilience by adding jobs and extending a six-and-a-half-year-long expansion, while inflation is too high.

fragments.text: GDP expanded at a 2.4 percent pace in the first half of this year, roughly consistent with growth for the previous two years.

fragments.text: the unemployment rate has moved roughly sideways this year and ticked down to 4.1 percent in August.

fragments.text: The 12-month change in the personal consumption expenditures price index, the blue line in figure 6, was 3.4 percent in August.

summary.text: Governor Jefferson says the 12-month change in the personal consumption expenditures price index was 3.4 percent in August and remains concerned about higher energy prices raising inflation more broadly.

fragments.text: As my base case, I expect inflation to be elevated in the short run before resuming its decline toward our 2 percent goal as the effects of energy and other price shocks fade.
